nearest_prior_results.reference: Ruhollah Majdoddin, arXiv:2610.17420v1 (2026), Theorem 19.17 and Corollary 19.25; Model and Open Problem 19.26
nearest_prior_results.verified_result: The existing deterministic algorithm covers every compact abelian group of exponent dividing p^2 for each fixed prime p, uniformly in c. The stated open question concerns all bounded exponents. The explicit p^2 embedding already includes Z4^d times F2^d.

The inherited support product works for homomorphisms pi,K whenever the explicitly enumerated middle subgroup contains K(ker pi). Its probe enumeration and failed-scan bounds do not alone choose suitable homomorphisms for every exponent.

nearest_prior_results.reference: Josh Alman and Virginia Vassilevska Williams, arXiv:2610.06783v1 (2026), Corollary 26, Section 4.1
nearest_prior_results.verified_result: For N>=D^18 and polynomially bounded integer matrix entries, preprocessing costs O(N^2/D^0.063), and each entry query costs O(D^0.437). At most N^2/sqrt(D) prescribed entries fit the preprocessing bound.

Every fixed abelian-group-representable finite relation has a finite-group representation, and its coordinatewise problem reduces to 3SUM over a power of that fixed group. Thus the full group theorem makes every such relation truly subquadratic uniformly in c. This reduction and corollary mechanism are prior.

nearest_prior_results.reference: Timothy M. Chan, Reina Itakura, Zhiyuan Ma and Yuancheng Yu, arXiv:2610.42012v1 (30 October 2026), Theorem 2.3 and Sections 2.2/3
nearest_prior_results.verified_result: The recent integer-3SUM and odd-k-SUM algorithms use random-prime scalar hashing and carry-free encodings. They do not state the all-bounded-exponent group theorem and provide no immediate torsion-compatible replacement for its missing balancing argument.

substantive_delta: A bounded-time randomized witness algorithm now covers every fixed exponent bound M, including arbitrary higher prime powers and mixed-prime products, with delta_M=min(1/18,1/(8 ceil(log_2 M)))*(63/1000)/2 independent of the polynomial order exponent c. Simultaneous profiles based on ORIGINAL coset sizes and a least-row-count/extremal-divisor certificate control both deterministic label branching and expected survivors across every nonzero order layer.
why_nonroutine: The prior support-product lemma requires a small middle subgroup, few classes/probes and few false positives simultaneously; applying it with a fixed hash does not achieve those conditions in non-elementary torsion groups. The frozen proof supplies a new joint selection invariant rather than assuming recursive heavy-case bounds or importing integer hashes. The certificate upper-bounds e^ell using one tight divisor while lower-bounding d^ell for all divisors, and original-coset profiles avoid fragmentation errors. This yields the full missing class and is not a routine corollary of the cited p^2 theorem or matrix primitive.
significance: The result provides a uniform algorithmic primitive for the full bounded-exponent abelian matching class, with honest witness recovery and per-random-path cost bounds. Through the verified prior finite-representation reduction it also closes the sufficient tractability direction for every fixed group-representable finite coordinate relation. That is substantive structural and algorithmic value beyond a special case, although competitive STOC depth and broader impact remain uncertain and are assessed separately as working_paper.
